headline: Charter panel reviews budget rules, including the $2.1 million capital set-aside and Finance Committee role
summary: The minimum capital set-aside is $2.1 million a year from the operating budget, and larger projects are usually paid for by bonds. Members discussed whether to raise that minimum, and whether to add members of the public or a fifth member to the Finance Committee. A public speaker said delayed audits are holding up a $6 million recreation bond. The commission also voted 5-3 to send City Council a recommendation on outside legal counsel.
decisions: Recommended that City Council accept the lower-cost of two outside law firm bids, 5-3, with legal requests going through the chair.
discussion: Capital set-aside minimum: Views differed on whether the $2.1 million minimum, about 0.05% of the budget, should rise. Some suggested doubling or tripling it, and others suggested asking the Capital Projects Committee for input first.

Finance and Budget Committee roles: The Finance Committee has four members who approve individual spending and monitor the budget, while the full council acts as the Budget Committee. Ideas raised included adding public members, adding a fifth member, and requiring regular reports to the council.

Audit timing and penalties: Members said the annual audit requirement is clear but has no deadline or consequence for missing it. Some wanted a timetable and enforcement, while others said the charter should stay as written.
Budget public input: Ideas included ward budget meetings before the budget vote, a budget message summarizing the plan, and a share of 1%, 5%, or 10% of the budget set aside for public voting.

Outside legal counsel: Views were split on whether the commission needs outside lawyers, with some saying the city solicitor could handle questions. The commission then voted on a recommendation to City Council.

decision_evidence.quote: Motion to accept the lower cost of the two bids for outside council. Seconded. So we'll motion that we recommend to council that we accept the lower of the two bids discussion. ...So it passes five to three with the chair opting not to vote.

decision_titles: Outside legal counsel for the Charter Commission
